evidence: Cic. Fam. 5.12.7: neque pictam neque fictam imāginem suam passus est esse (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A likeness of a person in any medium, with the genitive of the sitter (imāgō Āfricānī). Add picta for a painting, as against a bust or statue (ficta); imāginēs are also the wax masks of a Roman family’s ancestors. It has other common senses too: a reflection, an image in the mind, a ghost (see picture).

evidence: Cic. N.D. 1.103: effigiēs hominis et imāgō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A copy that resembles its original, a likeness; more formal than imāgō.

phrases.latin: similem esse tē volō quōmodo fīlium, nōn quōmodo imāginem: imāgō rēs mortua est
phrases.english: I want you to resemble me as a son does, not as a portrait does: a portrait is a dead thing
